title: This week in 5 numbers: Workers would spend up to $2,500 on their own training
summary: Here’s a roundup of numbers from the last week — including how many jobs robots physically can complete on a cost-competitive basis.

title: Employee benefits seem to satisfy workers, but gaps persist
summary: While workers have reported higher well-being since 2019, WTW found financial concerns are straining workers’ access to medical care.

title: Walmart plans to offer employees free prescriptions, paid NICU leave
summary: The news comes as employers prepare for nearly double-digit health insurance price increases and many plan to shift some of those costs to workers.

title: Leaders say they are worried about their ability to handle change
summary: Companies are facing a workplace confidence problem as technology develops rapidly, new research shows.

title: CEOs want ‘enterprise CHROs’ who can talk strategy and skills, report finds
summary: As AI transforms work, enterprise CHROs in high-performing companies are partnering with senior tech leaders, according to Heidrick & Struggles.

title: Robots can handle a third of physical jobs — but not yet cost-effectively, Anthropic says
summary: About 300,000 jobs are exposed today; 2.8 million could be at risk in seven years, says an analysis by the AI company.

title: Time spent waiting to work is compensable if required, appeals court rules
summary: Lidl employees can continue with their allegations they were required to report to work but couldn’t clock in until a manager unlocked the store.

title: Mailbag: How can HR keep track of employees’ credentials?
summary: Artificial intelligence could have multiple potential applications in this space, according to HR industry veteran Josh Bersin.

title: More ‘even-handed’: Understanding EEOC’s direction on national origin bias
summary: Under Trump 2.0, the agency has shifted its focus to anti-American bias rather than discrimination against immigrants.

title: HR leaders may be able to use AI to improve employee wellness
summary: Nearly half of workers have been reluctant to use artificial intelligence, but a study from Gartner found the technology may be useful in identifying burnout.
